Messages.Author: Gary J Rondeau
Messages.Body:
Is it possible to play a sudden reversal on a sudden reversal?
Our current house rule is no.
If so, is the original master card back in effect?

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
ad...@rgfn.epcc.edu (Gary J Rondeau) writes:

>Is it possible to play a sudden reversal on a sudden reversal?
>Our current house rule is no.

Yes (by another Methuselah whose turn it isn't). This second SR can be
SR'ed again by a third Methuselah whose turn it isn't. And so on.

>If so, is the original master card back in effect?

Naturally.

Messages.Author: Gord Culleton
Messages.Body:
Gary J Rondeau (ad...@rgfn.epcc.edu) writes:
> Is it possible to play a sudden reversal on a sudden reversal?
> Our current house rule is no.

Why not? As long as the Meth. playing the *original* master isn't
the Meth. playing the 2nd SR, there should be no problem. An SR
is a master, after all...
